# PR #3761: Patch: the AI Floats mana on purpose to bring its Float-discount cards within reach

Closes #3695

## Summary

The AI now gives credit for mana it leaves unspent at the end of a turn (a Float) when that mana brings a "Float reduces cost" card in its own hand closer to castable. The mechanism works in the tests, and the smoke gate is unchanged. **One acceptance item is not met: the issue's sweep shows no more casts than before.** The sweep numbers are below.

## What changed

- **Engine.**
  - `TriggerDef` has a new flag, `lowers_cost_on_float`. Only `float::float_reduces_cost` sets it.
  - The new `float::float_cuts_in_hand` reads, from the scripts the engine registers, what a Float of n takes off each hand card. A fused card keeps the flag.
  - Every `TriggerDef { … }` literal gets `lowers_cost_on_float: false`: `twice_forward.rs`, cards c064 and c071, and the twice-forward rules fixture that main's #3696 added.
- **AI.**
  - New weight `AI_EVAL.float_discount` at 0.8, the same as `unspent_mana`; `GREEDY_EVAL` keeps 0.
  - `evaluate::float_credit` pays the weight for each Floated crystal that went toward an own Float card still costing more than the seat's `mana.max`. Each card counts only up to its remaining distance, and the handicap is never read (R180).
  - Both places that score a passed line add it: `passed_score` and `replied_score`.
  - The effect: a crystal Floated toward a card out of reach now nets +0.5 instead of −0.3, and one Floated past that distance still costs −0.3.
- **Spec.**
  - New ruling `R3695000` with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/3695.md`.
  - §9.9's Evaluation bullet names the credit.
  - The AI README has a new paragraph.
- **Merge.** I resolved a conflict in `spec/09-architecture.md`, keeping main's #3696 reply bullet and this branch's Evaluation insert. It is staged, not committed.

## Tests

- `crates/cards/tests/cross/float_cuts.rs` has 2 tests of the engine read.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/float_discount.rs` has 7 tests: the issue's evaluation test (both halves), exact tests of the credit, the reply path, the two decision tests the issue asks for, and a test of a Float the credit causes.
- I switched the credit off and re-ran them. Four fail: the reply test, the score test, the credit test and the Float test. The two decision tests the issue asks for (Drone Core IX beside a one-drop; Drone Core X in reach with a free zone) pass either way. They stand as guards.
- Commands run, all passing:
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: 35, 821 and 98 tests. 7 were skipped; none were marked to skip by this change.
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit`
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `patches check`, `names --check` and `spec check`
- I did not run the full workspace test command with `jackioh-engine/ts`, or the web tests. The harness runs those.

## Gate and sweep (main `e8dfc7a2b7` against this branch, same machine)

- **`cargo jackioh gate` passes,** identical at both:

  | Gate | Wins | Needed |
  |---|---|---|
  | ai-vs-random | 19 of 20 | 17 |
  | ai-vs-greedy | 16 of 20 | 10 |
  | hard-vs-easy | 20 of 20 | 16 |

  The perf gate's slowest decision was about 41 ms at both.
- **`cargo jackioh sweep stinkyscape-033 stinkyscape-034 stinkyscape-035 stinkyscape-036`:**
  - Pass 1 flagged none of the four Drone Cores at either difficulty.
  - The pass-1 numbers come from the same seeds run with `--json`. Drone Core VII, VIII and IX are identical before and after, and so is X at Hard.
  - Each cell below is drawn games, turns X was affordable, and casts.

  | Drone Core X | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Easy, pass 1 (8 games) | 5/8, 1, 1 | 5/8, 3, 2 |
  | Easy, pass 2 (24 games) | 12/24, 2, 1 | 12/24, 1, 0 |
  | Hard, pass 2 (24 games) | 16/24, 4, 0 | 16/24, 3, 0 |

- **Overall it is 13 casts of the four cards before and 13 after.** The 2026-10-29 report had Drone Core X cast once at Easy (1 affordable turn) and once at Hard (18 affordable turns). This sweep shows no more casts.

## Why the sweep doesn't move: the second cause, reported and not fixed

- When Drone Core X is in reach with a free unit zone, the AI casts it at Easy and Hard on every seed tried. Hard's crystals reach 7, so X is one Float away, yet it still leaves X in hand.
- The Drone Battleship enters as one Stack pile (R1842000). Only its top layer, a 12/12 that can't attack, is scored. The two dormant layers under it score `dormant_share`, which is 0 since #1506's screen.
- I measured what casting X gains on a bare Hard board: +14.4 at `dormant_share` 0, +32.9 at 0.5, +51.5 at 1.0.
- Changing that already-screened weight moves the score of every Stack pile, so it is not the small fix the issue allows here. **A person should decide whether Stack piles' dormant layers should count (#1506).**

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **The reach is the seat's `mana.max`.** I rejected `duos::next_turn_mana` (the earlier plan's reach) because it reads the handicap, which the evaluation must never do (R180).
- **Float cards are found by a flag on the trigger,** not a hand-written list, so fused cards are covered.
- **Two Float cards in hand each count their own distance.** I rejected counting only the largest cut.
- **The weight stays at 0.8.** I tried 2.4 on X's pass 1: Easy 2 affordable turns and 2 casts, Hard 4 and none. That is no better, with more risk of hoarding mana.
- **Not changed:** `hand_cost_cap` (it moves every card's hand price) and `dormant_share` (above).

## Worth a second look

- **Unverified by me:** run 1 found that on 7 crystals the AI prefers Genn (4) 14/14 or Greaser (2) 7/7 over Drone Core X. I re-measured the 14.4 / 32.9 / 51.5 gains but not that comparison.
- **Known approximations (listed in the ruling):**
  - Below the mana cap, `mana.max` can count one crystal the next refresh would have covered.
  - The Float is read from the turn log's unspent mana, which a trap firing at end of turn could make differ from the end-of-turn event's.
  - A Float card that reaches the hand after the turn ends is credited a cut it never got.

# #3695: Patch: the AI Floats mana on purpose to bring its Float-discount cards within reach
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some of the game's biggest cards cost more than anyone can ever have in one turn, and get cheaper each time their owner ends a turn with mana left over (a Float). A human player saves mana on purpose for a turn or two to land a 12/12 Battleship. The practice AI never does, because it scores leftover mana as pure waste, so these cards sit dead in its hand. Once this is built, the AI counts unspent mana as bringing such a card closer, and a player will see it hold back a turn and then drop its giant.

## Why
- Mana caps at 4 (`MAX_MANA`, `crates/engine/src/config.rs:41`; SPEC §2.3). Seven cards carry "Float reduces cost" (`float_reduces_cost`; SPEC §6 Float, R464, R1563000): Drone Core VII to X (5, 6, 6 and 8 mana; `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c033`–`c036`), GIGA Glowy Jelly Bean and Snom Bunny Mind Control (`crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c029`, `c049`) and YileGPT Prime (8 mana, `crates/cards/src/scripts/meditative/c049_1_yilegpt_unleashed.rs`).
- The AI charges `AI_EVAL.unspent_mana` (0.8 a crystal, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:652`) on every passed line (`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs:727`) and after every reply (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:618`), but prices a discount on a hand card at `hand_cost_delta` (0.5 a crystal, `config.rs:589`, read at `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:562`). With one Float card in hand every crystal Floated scores −0.3, whether or not the discount is what puts the card within reach.
- The hand prices an 8-cost card as a 6-cost one (`hand_cost_cap: 6.0`, `config.rs:582`) whatever the mana cap, so how far a card is from castable never enters the score.
- The sweep shows it. Drone Core X at Hard: drawn in 27 of 58 games, within mana on 18 turns, cast once (`training/history/sweep-2026-10-29-4.md:249`); the day before, within mana on 3 turns of 8 games and never cast (`training/history/sweep-2026-10-28.md:42`). `crates/ai/tests/ai/shadow_ban.rs:514-516` notes that Easy never brings GIGA Glowy Jelly Bean down to its four crystals by Floating.

## Proposal
- An engine read, in `crates/engine/src/query.rs` with its test (CLAUDE.md, Architecture: a missing board fact goes into the engine), of what a Float of n would take off each of a seat's hand cards, read from their hand triggers.
- A new weight, `AI_EVAL.float_discount`, pricing each crystal a line's Float takes off a hand card that still costs more than the seat's crystals. It starts at or above `unspent_mana`, stays 0 in `GREEDY_EVAL`, and goes through the gate like any weight change.
- The sweep's second number, 18 turns within mana and one cast, may have a second cause. A decision test with Drone Core X in reach and a free unit zone finds it: fixed here if small, reported in the pull request if not.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/query.rs` (or `float.rs`), `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/evaluate.rs` and a decision test beside it
- SPEC §2.3, §6 (Float), §10.7; R464, R1563000

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An evaluation test: with a Float card above the seat's crystals in hand, a passed line that Floats F scores no lower than the same line with no Float card in hand; with no Float card in hand, every score is as before.
- [ ] A decision test: an Easy seat on 4 crystals, holding Drone Core IX and a 1-cost 1/1 against an empty board, ends its turn with crystals left, and next turn casts Drone Core IX.
- [ ] A decision test: with Drone Core X within reach and a free unit zone, the AI casts it.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes, and `cargo jackioh sweep stinkyscape-033 stinkyscape-034 stinkyscape-035 stinkyscape-036` shows more casts than the 2026-10-29 report; both numbers are in the pull request.

## Size and risks
Medium: one engine read, one weight and its pricing, three or four tests. Set too high, the weight makes the AI hoard mana instead of building a board; it applies only while a card is still out of reach, and the gate guards the rest. It changes how the AI plays, so the gate's games are its real test.

## Goal

When the AI ends a turn with crystals unspent (a Float), it counts each crystal that brought a "Float reduces cost" card in its own hand closer to castable. So it holds mana back for a turn and then casts the card. Done means:
1. An engine read of what a Float of n takes off each of a seat's hand cards, taken from the hand triggers the engine registers.
2. A weight `AI_EVAL.float_discount` (0.8, the same as `unspent_mana`; 0 in `GREEDY_EVAL`), credited on every passed line for each Floated crystal that went toward a card still above the seat's crystals.
3. The issue's three tests, plus exact unit tests.
4. `cargo jackioh gate` green, the sweep run before and after, and the sweep's second cause reported. The planner found that cause, and it is not small (see Risks).
